title: Choosing models and interpreting excess mortality
text: reporting period: excess deaths=observed deaths−expected deaths \text{excess deaths} = \text{observed deaths} - \text{expected deaths} P-score=100×observed deaths−expected deathsexpected deaths. \text{P-score} = 100 \times \frac{\text{observed deaths} - \text{expected deaths}}{\text{expected deaths}}. Positive excess means deaths estimated baseline. Negative excess means . P-score expresses difference percentage expected deaths. population mortality rate. synthetic arithmetic example, fitted model: April, 1,230 observed deaths 1,000 expected deaths give 230 excess deaths P-score 23%. expected deaths zero, P-score undefined; small expected counts can make unstable.
code: illustration <- tibble(   month = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-02-01", "2020-03-01",                     "2020-04-01", "2020-05-01", "2020-06-01")),   observed_deaths = c(980, 1010, 1120, 1230, 1190, 1060),   expected_deaths = c(1000, 1000, 1000, 1000, 1000, 1000) )  illustration <- illustration |>   mutate(     excess_deaths = observed_deaths - expected_deaths,     p_score = if_else(expected_deaths > 0,                       100 * excess_deaths / expected_deaths, NA_real_)   ) illustration #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   month      observed_deaths expected_deaths excess_deaths p_score #>   <date>               <dbl>           <dbl>         <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 2020-01-01             980            1000           -20      -2 #> 2 2020-02-01            1010            1000            10       1 #> 3 2020-03-01            1120            1000           120      12 #> 4 2020-04-01            1230            1000           230      23 #> 5 2020-05-01            1190            1000           190      19 #> 6 2020-06-01            1060            1000            60       6 plot_data <- illustration |>   select(month, observed_deaths, expected_deaths) |>   pivot_longer(-month, names_to = "series", values_to = "deaths") |>   mutate(series = recode(series,                          observed_deaths = "Observed", expected_deaths = "Expected"))  ggplot(plot_data, aes(month, deaths, colour = series, linetype = series)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +   geom_point(size = 2) +   scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +   theme_dsi() +   labs(title = "Observed deaths and a counterfactual baseline",        subtitle = "Synthetic illustration; these are not country estimates",        x = NULL, y = "Deaths", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)

what: exmort — All-Cause and Excess Mortality Calculator
title: exmort — All-Cause and Excess Mortality Calculator
text: -Cause Excess Mortality Calculator — R Shiny application estimating -cause mortality excess mortality country-level weekly monthly death counts, developed Regional Office Western Pacific (WPRO). supply observed deaths event calendar (e.g. COVID-19 waves, typhoons). app fits one statistical baseline models using periods outside supplied events, estimates expected deaths across observed series, reports excess deaths, P-scores confidence limits tables, plots downloadable reports. Baseline models included: Historical average Negative binomial regression Quasi-Poisson regression Zero-inflated Poisson ARIMA / SARIMA Generalized additive model (GAM spline) Karlinsky–Kobak model Documentation: https://shanlong-.github.io/exmort/

Includes seven baseline models (historical average, negative binomial, quasi-Poisson, zero-inflated Poisson, ARIMA/SARIMA, GAM spline Karlinsky–Kobak model), event annotation, best-fit AIC comparison, HTML / Word / PDF report generation. Application code sourced private environment instead global environment, app longer leaves options(digits) LC_TIME locale changed session ends. Adds testthat suite covering ISO year-week date helpers, model date index upload validators.
